mappings.note: What GDP shows. An economic concept, but neither LO fits -- LO-1 is sector classification and LO-2 is organised/unorganised work -- so the C-4.1 competency (recalls and understands economic concepts and indicators). Reported as a frame gap: the GDP strand of this chapter has no outcome.

Which organisation runs the five-yearly employment and unemployment survey. Recall of the statistical apparatus, C-4.1. Not C-4.3, which would need the data itself to be analysed rather than the collector named.

Identify the NATURAL product from a list -- the test of whether an activity or good comes straight from nature, i.e. the primary sector. LO-1. NOTE for the reader: this chapter's outcome codes are bare LO-1 and LO-2, not the C-4.1-LO-n form used in chapter 23700.
Which example does NOT fall under the unorganised sector -- LO-2 is the organised/unorganised outcome. Not LO-1: no primary/secondary/tertiary judgement is involved.

Who owns Tisco and Reliance (the private sector). The public/private division is a third classification in this chapter and has NO learning outcome -- LO-1 is primary/secondary/tertiary and LO-2 is organised/unorganised -- so C-4.1 competency. Reported as a frame gap.
The number of days NREGA guarantees (100). A statutory protection for workers, which is the second half of LO-2. Not LO-1: no sector is being classified.

When underemployment occurs -- people at work but producing less than they could. A condition of employment, so LO-2's analysis of work and the need to protect workers. Not LO-1, although underemployment is concentrated in one sector; the item defines the condition.
Which sector has become the largest producing sector (tertiary) -- a statement about the three-sector division, LO-1.

Where DISGUISED unemployment is found most. The subject is hidden unemployment among workers, LO-2; the answer happens to name agriculture, but the concept tested is the employment condition, not the classification.

How big private companies contribute to national development -- the student reasons about a real-world effect rather than recalling a classification. C-4.2 (applies economic reasoning to everyday situations). Neither LO covers the public/private strand.
Which activity does NOT belong to the primary sector -- sector classification, LO-1.
Which sector is the largest EMPLOYER in India (primary) -- a fact about the three-sector division, LO-1. Not LO-2: employment share by sector is not the organised/unorganised distinction.
Who measures GDP -- the GDP strand again, with no LO behind it. C-4.1 competency.
Life insurance belongs to the tertiary sector -- classification, LO-1.
The motive of public sector enterprises (public welfare, not profit). Public/private, which has no LO in this chapter; C-4.1 competency.
The money value of all final goods and services produced in a year -- the definition of GDP. C-4.1 competency, since the GDP strand has no outcome.
Which economic activity does not come under the primary sector -- classification, LO-1.
Which activity is not a primary-sector activity -- classification, LO-1. A near-duplicate of the item above and mapped the same way.
What is meant by GDP -- the definitional item again, C-4.1 competency.
Agriculture and dairy farming belong to the primary sector -- classification, LO-1.
Which condition does NOT apply to an organised-sector worker -- the item turns on the protections (fixed hours, paid leave, provident fund) that mark organised employment. LO-2 exactly.

The motive of public sector enterprises -- a duplicate of an earlier item in this same chapter, mapped identically at C-4.1 because the public/private strand has no LO. DEFECT: two byte-different but substantively identical questions are stored in the same chapter.
Which activity is NOT in the tertiary sector -- classification, LO-1.
What the service sector includes -- the content of the tertiary sector, LO-1.
Which activities the secondary sector covers -- classification, LO-1.
The days of employment guaranteed by NREGA 2005 -- worker protection, LO-2. A duplicate of the earlier NREGA item; mapped consistently.
Information and communication technology belongs to the tertiary sector -- classification, LO-1.
In which sector activities are not guided by profit (the public sector). Public/private again, with no LO; C-4.1 competency.
Manufacturing belongs to the secondary sector -- classification, LO-1.
What the primary sector relates to -- classification, LO-1.

Who carries out economic activities. A very general concept item with no sector classification and no employment condition in it, so C-4.1 competency. DEFECT: the stem is so bare that the intended answer cannot be inferred from the row; the options are not stored.

The basis on which the economy is split into public and private (ownership of assets and provision of services). The public/private strand, which has no LO, so C-4.1 competency. Not LO-2, whose division is organised against unorganised -- a different cut of the same economy and a common confusion this item is probably testing.
